question: Before a 49-year-old man, asymptomatic, with a family history of a father who died of prostate cancer, a PSA (Specific Prostate Antigen) of 5.9 ng / ml was identified in a routine company control, with a PSA ratio free / Total PSA of 11% and that in a digital rectal examination there is an increase in consistency in the right prostatic lobe, what is the following clinical indication?

options.opa: Ask the patient to perform a transrectal ultrasound and prostate biopsy.
options.opc: Start treatment with 5 alpha reductase inhibitors to halve PSA levels.
options.opd: Start combined treatment of LHRH analogues and antiandrogens.
